A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExploreVLA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing content can be matched across reflow and renumbering, and the added experiments are identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original NAVSIM results, component ablations and qualitative planning/generation outcomes, plus nuScenes results in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds trajectory-perturbation experiments, safety-threshold sensitivity results and closed-loop HUGSIM evaluation.

M1.justification: The backbone, joint trajectory/RGB/depth prediction, safety-gated exploration reward and GRPO training remain unchanged. Specifying the entropy-normalization function adds implementation detail; the PDFs do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds fully reactive HUGSIM evaluation across KITTI-360, Waymo, nuScenes and PandaSet source domains. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained non-reactive NAVSIM and open-loop nuScenes settings, including conditions where the policy's actions affect subsequent states.

E2.justification: The new HUGSIM comparison uses a distinct three-comparator lineup: VAD, UniAD and LTF (Table 8). LTF cites the same reference used for TransFuser elsewhere, so it should not automatically be treated as an entirely new algorithm. Comparator membership in the original NAVSIM and nuScenes comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot reactive rollouts measured by HD-Score, without closed-loop fine-tuning or domain adaptation. It also adds speed-versus-direction perturbations on 1,000 randomly selected straight-driving scenes and a safety-threshold sweep over 0, 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9. Previously documented training budgets, splits and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 supplements the existing correlation plot and qualitative novelty example with a controlled 1,000-scene diagnostic (Table 3). Section 4.4 adds safety-threshold sensitivity analysis (Table 6), while Appendix B.3 probes transfer to reactive conditions and identifies a Waymo weakness. Existing component ablations and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 newly reports ± quantities for L2 error and exploration bonus. Their statistical meaning is not defined, and neither version reports repeated-run counts or seeds. This establishes added spread/uncertainty reporting, but not additional runs or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing table scores are unchanged. New Table 3 reports speed/direction perturbation L2 values of 5.82±1.74 versus 2.15±0.93 and bonuses of 0.04±0.03 versus 0.29±0.12. Table 6 adds threshold-dependent PDMS results. Table 8 newly reports ExploreVLA HD-Scores of 0.105, 0.360, 0.517 and 0.821: first on KITTI-360, third on Waymo and second on nuScenes and PandaSet among the listed methods. These are additional findings, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: After Eq. (6), v2 explicitly defines f(H) = (H-Hmin)/(Hmax-Hmin), whereas v1 only states that f bounds the bonus within [0,1]. This adds a mathematical specification of the previously unspecified mapping. The remaining equations are unchanged, with no added theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and main conclusion retain the same claims about dense RGB/depth supervision, uncertainty-guided exploration and state-of-the-art NAVSIM performance, including PDMS 93.7 and EPDMS 88.8. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains weak sensitivity to lower safety thresholds using the finding that approximately 99% of sampled trajectories already exceed PDMS 0.6. It attributes the Waymo shortfall to limited recovery experience under offline/open-loop training. The conclusion replaces the proposed BEV-supervision extension with this concrete limitation and a closed-loop RL direction, while retaining the single-camera limitation.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 now specifies min-max entropy normalization. The abstract replaces a future code-and-demo release promise with a statement that code is available at the same project address; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Appendix A's backbone, preprocessing, hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the HUGSIM reference to support the new simulator evaluation and metric. Existing cited works and the substantive positioning in Section 2 are retained; subsequent reference renumbering does not represent additional citation changes.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits in the introduction and related work, expanded experimental discussion, a new Appendix B.3 and revised limitations. Author contact information and an internship footnote are added, and the keyword 'World model' becomes 'World action model.' The main organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables for perturbation statistics, threshold sensitivity and HUGSIM results (Tables 3, 6 and 8). Existing tables are renumbered and redistributed, and Figure 4 is resized. All six figures retain their content, and the overall visual format is preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central exploration mechanism: the earlier qualitative novelty example gains a 1,000-scene controlled test and a safety-threshold study. HUGSIM adds previously absent reactive closed-loop evidence, including a Waymo weakness that motivates a more informative limitation. These address important evidential gaps in v1, although undefined ± statistics and limited closed-loop protocol detail still constrain interpretation and reproducibility.
